extracted.intended_audience: college mathematics instructors, curriculum designers, and assessment specialists interested in quantitative literacy courses
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and assessment practices for designing, delivering, and evaluating first-year quantitative literacy (general education) mathematics courses for non-technical majors, with emphasis on engagement, technology, writing, and measurable learning outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of placement test baseline
rubrics_metrics.description: The placement test data was used to generate a baseline percentage for each of the previously mentioned topics. The baseline represents the number of students beginning a mathematics course with an understanding of that particular topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each topic, combine data for the questions related to that topic and compare the proportion answering correctly on the placement test (baseline) with the proportion answering correctly on post-test items; use this baseline for measuring course impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-test items embedded on final exam
rubrics_metrics.description: Four different questions were included on each of the four versions of the placement test. The same four questions on each version were used in four post-test versions included as the last page of the final exams of general education mathematics courses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed identical/same-format items from baseline instruments on final exams as post-tests to measure gains; ensure items are distributed so versions are comparable in difficulty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical comparison of proportions with significance threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: A statistical comparison was conducted of the proportion of students answering the topic-related questions correctly with the proportion of students who took the placement test and answered the questions correctly on the final exam. A significant result (p < .05) was obtained when the proportion on the final exam was statistically larger than the placement test proportion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use inferential statistics (proportion tests) and adopt a clear alpha threshold (here p < .05) to declare significant gains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement test scoring rule (penalty for incorrect answers)
rubrics_metrics.description: A placement level is generated by the number of correct responses on the placement test minus one-fourth of the number of incorrect responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for scoring rules that may discourage guessing; document how scoring affects item response rates and baseline percentages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance and tracking of no-response/blanks
rubrics_metrics.description: The instructions state that it is acceptable for students to not answer any questions that they are uncertain about. As a result, several questions had a large number of no responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track and report item nonresponse rates by topic; analyze whether blank rates differ across courses or topics (e.g., counting principles had 64% blanks) and consider their impact on comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparing like cohorts across course sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Since Contemporary Mathematics and College Algebra have the same placement level, we decided to compare the assessment results of students in these two courses to determine relative effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure cohorts begin with similar baselines before attributing differences to course effects; statistically compare placement-test percentages to confirm similarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of multiple-choice-only assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: One limitation of the assessment method used to date is that it relies totally on multiple-choice responses, and does not allow for analysis beyond the five response items provided for each question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge that MC formats limit insight into reasoning; plan complementary assessments (open-ended items, interviews) to probe methods and deeper understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan to include open-ended items and interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: We have plans to develop an assessment for analyzing student responses to open-ended quantitative literacy questions. We also believe that a lot can be learned about student quantitative reasoning skills through interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Augment multiple-choice post-tests with constructed-response assessment and cognitive interviews to capture reasoning processes and possibly different results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of time-on-course self-report as an engagement metric
rubrics_metrics.description: A multiple-choice question asked students to estimate, on average, the total time they spend on this course (including class, tests, quizzes, assignments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include simple self-report items about time spent to triangulate engagement; analyze by course and by rank/grade as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course completion and grade distributions as success indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: The percentage of students successfully completing the course (receiving an A, B, or C) and withdrawal rates were compared between Contemporary Mathematics and College Algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report completion (A/B/C) rates and withdrawal rates as measures of course effectiveness and student success; consider instructor opinions and other contextual factors when interpreting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on specific course goals for assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: This assessment primarily focused on aspects of the first two goals of Contemporary Mathematics; main differences in other course goals could not be assessed through this series of multiple-choice questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map assessment instruments explicitly to articulated course goals and recognize when some goals are not captured by chosen assessment methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Just-in-time instruction philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty use the 'just-in-time' philosophy when covering mathematics topics: All concepts are reviewed or introduced as needed to solve real-life problems, rather than using problems solely to motivate the learning of algebraic manipulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design instruction so topics are introduced in direct response to problem-solving needs; emphasize contextualized learning over decontextualized procedure practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of technology (labs, applets, WebCT) for practice, exploration, and feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Most labs incorporate technology to solve problems. Drill and exploration via Java applets and on-line quizzes (WebCT) provide instant feedback and automatic grading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ interactive applets for guided drill and conceptual exploration; use LMS quizzes with parameterized problems for randomized practice and immediate feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quizzes as learning tools with repeat attempts and tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: WebCT quizzes can be designed with template forms and automatically graded parameter ranges; an approach is to allow five retakes with the highest score recorded. WebCT automates tracking of grades and records which problems were commonly missed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use automatically graded quizzes to create low-stakes iterative practice, allow multiple attempts, and use system logs to identify common misconceptions and problem items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guided drill and interactive exploration via applets
rubrics_metrics.description: Drill exercises where students choose formula, enter values, compute and receive instant feedback; interactive exploration applets (e.g., histogram slider) illustrate effects of parameter choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide both guided drill (procedural fluency) and exploratory applets (conceptual understanding) and collect student feedback on usability and learning value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate writing across curriculum (technical writing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many labs have a significant writing component to reflect 'writing across the curriculum'; write-ups take the form of reports to the poser of the problem and require appropriate presentation of technical information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require drafts with instructor feedback and revisions to develop technical writing skills; clarify expectations distinguishing technical writing from general composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of mini-topics to increase relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a series of week- to two-week mini-topics to show how mathematics links to student disciplines and to illustrate current questions in mathematics (examples: music tuning, cryptology, geometry of the earth).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rotate or substitute mini-topics tailored to section interests to increase engagement and show interdisciplinary connections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of core modules appropriate for non-technical majors
rubrics_metrics.description: The course includes four basic modules: physical measurement, personal finance, consumer statistics, and resource allocation. Instructors may choose to use all four or substitute mini-topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize modules that deliver practical, widely-relevant quantitative skills for non-technical majors (finance, statistics, measurement), while keeping options to customize content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking courses through freshman programs to increase engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Link MAT1010 with other freshman programs (FIG, Watauga College) and use shared themes or the summer reading program to create interdisciplinary connections and a sense of cohort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form FIG links or special sections tied to living-learning communities and shared readings to build relevance and student ownership; monitor faculty workload and behavioral dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty support and mentorship for new instructors
rubrics_metrics.description: Experienced MAT1010 faculty are assigned to help orient new instructors to the course philosophy and the lab component. A cadre of short-term instructors, part-time faculty and graduate assistants is developed and refreshed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide mentoring and orientation for adjuncts and new instructors to maintain course philosophy and quality in a staffing model that relies on part-time personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure student attitudes/pre-post attitudinal surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: End-of-course and pre/post surveys were used to measure improvements in student perceptions of math skills, computer comfort, perceived relevance of mathematics, math anxiety, and confidence with word problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include validated attitudinal measures administered before and after the course to capture changes in affective outcomes in addition to cognitive gains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use assessment data to refine course materials
rubrics_metrics.description: We are pleased with the improvement but also are working to modify the course in order to further increase the number of students able to successfully answer quantitative literacy questions of this type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use item- and topic-level assessment results to iteratively revise curriculum and instruction; target topics with low gains or high nonresponse for redesign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document constraints and interpret results cautiously
rubrics_metrics.description: One limitation is reliance on multiple-choice responses; some course goals could not be assessed; instructor opinion and student engagement may influence outcomes like course grades.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report limitations explicitly (instrument format, unmeasured goals, nonrandom instructor effects) and avoid overgeneralizing from limited measures.
